findings.issue: The app ships no test suite at all — no runner, no test script, no spec files — despite the framework's own starters including test-suite setups and the code being factored into pure, testable modules.
findings.suggestion: Add vitest (works out of the box with the existing vite.config.ts) and a test script covering app/src/lib/browse.ts, app/src/lib/format.ts and the transform helpers in data.ts with fixture JSON.

findings.issue: browse() — case-insensitive substring on humanized labels, type-in-either-slot, generation match, 48/page slicing and page clamping — is the core risk surface and untested; a refactor of SpeciesIndex (e.g. changing the `types` array shape) would break filtering silently.
findings.suggestion: Unit tests over a small synthetic SpeciesIndex covering each filter, combined filters, empty results (pageCount 0), and out-of-range page clamping.

findings.issue: moveRows() encodes subtle rules: dedup key `${method}|${name}|${level}` (level only for level-up — a Pokémon learning a move twice as 'machine' in different ways would wrongly dedupe), METHOD_ORDER ranking with alphabetical tie-break, and level-then-name sort. Nothing pins any of it.
findings.suggestion: Feed a fixture PokemonRecord/MoveRecord set through moveRows and assert table order, dedup behaviour and level nullability.

findings.issue: Client-side table sorting (missing values last in both directions, aria-sort flip, numeric vs collator compare, stable position tie-break) is DOM-only logic with zero coverage; the acceptance tests may not click every column in both directions.
findings.suggestion: A jsdom/Playwright component test that clicks each header twice and asserts row order and aria-sort; at minimum, extract the comparison into a pure function and unit-test it.

findings.issue: Live filtering has race-prone logic (ticket-based latest guard at line 42, 150 ms debounce, push vs replace history choice, fallback to location.assign on index fetch failure) that is exactly where regressions hide.
findings.suggestion: Playwright test: type quickly and assert only the final state renders and the URL ends up correct; failing /api/species-index falls back to a full navigation.

findings.issue: URL state round-trip (stateFromParams/stateToSearch) has edge cases: parseInt accepts '?page=3x' as 3, negative/zero pages fall back to 1, and defaults must be omitted. Untested.
findings.suggestion: Property-style unit tests: stateToSearch(stateFromParams(s)) normalises as specified for q/type/generation/page.

findings.issue: getSpeciesIndex() joins three API lists (species, 18 filtered types, generations) into the index entries; slot-order type assembly and generation assignment are unguarded — a mis-join would produce wrong cards for every list page.
findings.suggestion: Test with fixture JSON containing an alternate form, a dual-type Pokémon and a species with no generation entry, asserting entries, ordering and exclusion of ids > 10000.

findings.issue: cardsFor() — the alternate-form filter (id <= 10000, which also handles NaN URLs), dedup by species id, and the 'Hidden ability' note — is shared by move/ability/type pages and untested.
findings.suggestion: Unit test with refs including an id above 10000, a duplicate, and a hidden-ability note.

findings.issue: The runtime cache (60 s TTL, eviction of failed promises, >5000-entry sweep, 24-slot semaphore) is untested; a TTL or eviction regression could serve stale data across the live-data-overlay scenario the spec explicitly warns about.
findings.suggestion: Unit tests with a fake fetch asserting cache hits within TTL, re-fetch after expiry, and no caching of rejected promises.

findings.issue: Not-found handling depends on getByName's slug regex and 404→null mapping in load(); a bad name must render the Not found page, not a 500. Untested.
findings.suggestion: Tests for getByName with '', 'MISSINGNO', '../etc', and a name the API 404s, asserting null and thus the 404 route's rendering path.

summary: The agent wrote no tests of its own; the only guard is the external acceptance suite, which the rubric does not credit. The code is unusually well-factored for testing (pure, isomorphic lib modules), which makes the omission more costly than incidental. Every risky area — filtering, pagination, URL state, sorting, cache semantics, alternate-form exclusion, 404 paths — is untested, and any refactor of the data layer would ship regressions undetected.
